paper_title: MICROSCOPE mission: first constraints on the violation of the weak equivalence principle by a light scalar dilaton
coupling_convention: dimensionless Yukawa strength alpha (relative to gravity) for coupling to baryon number B, alpha_ij = alpha*(B/mu)_i*(B/mu)_j
notes: Paper uses MICROSCOPE's first Eotvos parameter measurement (eta = (-1 +/- 27)e-15 at 2-sigma) to constrain several scalar-field couplings: (1) Yukawa alpha with charge q=B: |alpha| < 1e-11 for m_phi < 1e-12 eV (extracted here, flat bound; lower mass edge set to 1e-18 eV as an approximate span since the bound saturates for light fields and no explicit lower limit is given); (2) q=B-L: |alpha| < 1e-12 (would map to VectorBL-like charge but as a scalar); (3) generic dilaton parameters (D_m, D_e); (4) electromagnetic-only dilaton d_e ~< 1e-4 for 1e-18 < m/eV < 1e-11 (ScalarPhoton-type). ScalarBaryon (q=B) chosen per the primary result and hint, but multiple coupling types are constrained, hence confidence <= 0.55. Not a dark-matter search; no DM density assumed.
